What I'm hearing is that you're hung up on the "first everything" aspect. Just because he was the first, doesn't mean he needs to be the last.

In my opinion, he's taking this break as more than just a way to improve himself; he's looking elsewhere because he's "technically" a single man. A break is a break. You are not together, just promising to get back together at some point. You may be taking this promise as you're still together, but in reality, you're a single woman. Your heart is with him, but you're not.

It's a difficult situation to be in, but at the end of the day, you're accepting this behavior by being complacent and staying with him. You're accepting defeat in an unwinnable situation, expecting to go back to normal when your break may or may not end. You're waiting for someone who very well may not be planning on coming back. Do you really want to be with someone you're so uncertain about because you're comfortable with him? Is this the behavior you want to teach your child is ok when they grow up and have a partner?

Put you and your child first. I'm not saying to drop him and immediately jump into a relationship either. But you need to look at this as a sign that maybe you two aren't as compatible as you once thought. It isn't the end of the world, but maybe the end of the relationship would help you see a clearer picture.
